newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY POLICE FINDS BOMB IN SUPERMARKET.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY POLICE FINDS BOMB IN SUPERMARKET.

text.p: Only quick police action may have saved Hungarians on Thursday from a potentially fatal new attack in a spate of bombings, the Hungarian Television said.
A pipe bomb hidden on a shelf in a usually crowded supermarket in the southwest Hungarian town Pecs was defused by the police, which had been warned by an unknown telephoner.
"The bomb could have caused serious damage in life and material," Mihaly Ernyes, police captain of Baranya county told the television.
Almost two dozen car showrooms, restaurants, pubs, nightclubs or peep shows have been damaged in Budapest since September by hand grenades or bombs.
At least three people have been shot to death in a mushrooming gang war, which is supposed by the police to be linked with many of the bombings.
Also on Thursday, a 25 year old man, was shot seven times in Budapest, and his injuries threaten his death, the television said.
"He is not unknown for the police," a police spokesman told the television.
